name: Generative AI for Cyber-Physical Systems
description: This course covers the application of generative AI to cyber-physical systems (CPS). Topics include generative architectures, variational autoencoders, generative adversarial networks, diffusion models, and large language models, applied to CPS tasks: synthetic sensor data generation, anomaly detection, autonomous decision-making via agentic AI, generative design of hardware and sensor networks, and AI-driven digital twins. Students learn to deploy generative models under real-time, resource-constrained, and safety-critical conditions inherent to CPS. Additional topics include edge deployment, hardware-aware optimization, security of generative systems, and ethical considerations for autonomous CPS.
prereq: No formal prerequisites. Recommended: Basic ML/DL knowledge (one introductory course, e.g. COL341/ELL784), Python proficiency, linear algebra and probability. B.Tech 3rd/4th year students may register with instructor approval.
